## Purpose and Entry Points
Webots is a cross-platform desktop robot simulator and development environment for modeling worlds, programming controllers, and simulating robots, vehicles, and mechanical systems. The native application starts at `src/webots/gui/main.cpp`; platform launch wrappers are under `src/webots/launcher/launcher.c` and `src/webots/launcher/webots-linux.sh`. The main build orchestration is `Makefile`, with the simulator build rooted at `src/webots/Makefile`.

## World Model, Parsing, and PROTO Composition
World (`.wbt`) and reusable PROTO (`.proto`) assets are parsed into a typed VRML-derived scene graph. Parsing, field values, node definitions, URLs, and serialization are concentrated in `src/webots/vrml/WbParser.cpp`, `src/webots/vrml/WbNodeFactory.cpp`, and `src/webots/vrml/WbProtoManager.cpp`. Concrete runtime nodes are created through `src/webots/nodes/utils/WbConcreteNodeFactory.cpp`; node classes model geometry, robots, devices, joints, materials, and physics, e.g. `src/webots/nodes/WbRobot.cpp` and `src/webots/nodes/WbSolid.cpp`.

## Simulation Runtime and Physics
A loaded world becomes a simulation world controlled by `src/webots/engine/WbSimulationWorld.cpp` and `src/webots/control/WbControlledWorld.cpp`. The simulation advances a coordinated loop: controllers submit actuator commands; nodes update state; ODE computes contacts, joints, and dynamics; sensors and rendering consume resulting state. The ODE integration boundary is `src/webots/ode/WbOdeContext.cpp` and `src/webots/ode/WbOdeUtilities.cpp`; the bundled physics engine and collision implementations live in `src/ode/ode/src/quickstep.cpp` and `src/ode/ode/src/collision_kernel.cpp`. Physics extensions are dynamically integrated through `src/webots/plugins/WbPhysicsPlugin.cpp`.

## Controller Process and Language APIs
Robot controllers run separately from the simulator and communicate through the controller runtime/protocol boundary. The controller executable launcher is `src/controller/launcher/webots_controller.c`; core C API scheduling and robot interaction are in `src/controller/c/scheduler.c`, `src/controller/c/robot.c`, and `src/controller/c/request.c`. Public C and C++ APIs are exposed by `include/controller/c/webots/robot.h` and `include/controller/cpp/webots/Robot.hpp`; Python bindings are distributed in `lib/controller/python/controller/robot.py`. Controllers read simulated devices/sensors and issue motor, communication, and supervisor commands each simulation step.

## Rendering and Native UI
The Qt-based desktop UI owns application lifecycle, scene editing, simulation controls, and views: `src/webots/gui/WbGuiApplication.cpp`, `src/webots/gui/WbMainWindow.cpp`, and `src/webots/gui/WbView3D.cpp`. Rendering maps simulation nodes into the Wren rendering layer, with adapters such as `src/webots/wren/WbWrenCamera.cpp`. Wren is an OpenGL-oriented renderer with scene, mesh, material, texture, shader, and framebuffer abstractions in `src/wren/Scene.cpp`, `src/wren/Renderable.cpp`, and `src/wren/ShaderProgram.cpp`; shader assets reside in `resources/wren/shaders/`.

## Web Streaming and Extensibility
Webots supports browser-side streamed viewing through JavaScript scene/node implementations and a client/server protocol. Browser orchestration is in `resources/web/wwi/WebotsView.js`, `resources/web/wwi/Stream.js`, and `resources/web/wwi/W3dScene.js`; the native streaming endpoints include `src/webots/gui/WbW3dStreamingServer.cpp` and `src/webots/gui/WbMultimediaStreamingServer.cpp`. Plugin boundaries cover physics, radio, remote control, and robot-window UIs via `include/plugins/physics.h`, `src/webots/plugins/WbPlugin.cpp`, and `resources/projects/plugins/robot_windows/generic/generic.js`.

## Content Library and External Integrations
`projects/` is the packaged simulation catalog: robot/device PROTOs, controllers, worlds, demonstrations, and benchmarks. Representative composition paths are `projects/robots/gctronic/e-puck/protos/E-puck.proto`, `projects/vehicles/protos/abstract/AckermannVehicle.proto`, and `projects/samples/robotbenchmark/`. Vehicle worlds integrate SUMO traffic networks/configuration, e.g. `projects/vehicles/worlds/city_net/sumo.sumocfg`, with the interface controller in `projects/default/controllers/sumo_supervisor/sumo_supervisor.py`. OpenStreetMap import/export tooling is implemented in `resources/osm_importer/importer.py` and `resources/sumo_exporter/exporter.py`.

## Build, Distribution, and Platform Boundaries
The codebase is primarily C/C++ with Qt, OpenGL/Wren, and bundled ODE; controller runtimes additionally support C, C++, Python, Java, and MATLAB. Dependency builds are OS-specific under `dependencies/Makefile.linux`, `dependencies/Makefile.mac`, and `dependencies/Makefile.windows`. Packaging and release assembly are handled by `scripts/packaging/webots_distro.py` and its OS-specific distro scripts.
